summary: Register MAX Bot API as a Social Core provider adapter with exact-channel bot authorization, released text/image/gallery/video publishing, HTTPS URL buttons, bounded status reads, production webhook secret verification and host-owned durable deduplication.

impacts.evidence: The adapter receives only a validated tenant-bound Account and one configured numeric ChatID. Publish receipts, status reads and webhook events must match that ChatID; no caller tenant/channel override exists.

Only bounded MAX chat/message identifiers and canonicalized admitted webhook payloads cross the provider boundary. Bot token and webhook verification secret remain callback-scoped behind SecretAccessor and are excluded from normalized errors/results.
Task 042 adds no public TORGNEXA HTTP/OpenAPI operation.
Task 042 adds no EventBus schema. The SocialWebhookReceiver result is an internal Connector SDK projection; host Task-009/EventBus wiring remains separately versioned.

Connector SDK v1 gains additive social.webhooks capability plus SocialWebhookRequest/Result/Receiver/Deduplicator types. Frozen Connector and Runtime roots are unchanged and existing providers need no implementation changes.
No migration is added. Durable webhook dedup is host-owned and must reuse tenant-scoped Task-009 Inbox/idempotency persistence rather than provider-local tables.

API authority is fixed, bot/channel identity is exact, secrets remain behind SecretAccessor, released media is re-opened through Task-088, dynamic media upload URLs use an exact HTTPS host allowlist, and webhook secret comparison is constant-time.

Task 042 admits publish/status/webhook surfaces only. Remote edit/delete and other destructive MAX operations remain undeclared; host Social Core authorization remains authoritative for publication dispatch.
Task-020 remains Content/Variant/Publication/audit/outbox authority. Provider results are bounded receipts and webhook projections; the adapter cannot mutate Core/audit/lineage stores directly.

Audited MAX send requests expose no caller idempotency token, so ambiguous writes fail closed as non-retryable write_outcome_unknown. Webhook retries are content-addressed from canonical JSON and claimed by host-owned durable dedup before processing.

Outbound API authority is platform-api2.max.ru; media upload egress is restricted to qualified official hosts. Production webhook subscription requires HTTPS implicit port 443, fixed update types and a separate verification secret; foreign/malformed events are rejected before dedup.

Manifest pacing is conservative against current provider guidance. Auth/permission/rate/service/write-unknown failures are normalized to bounded categories without raw provider messages or secret-bearing URLs.
Suspend the MAX connector account and delete its webhook subscription to stop new traffic. Existing canonical publication/audit/inbox evidence remains intact and no migration rollback is required.

Deterministic tests cover manifest/config/secrets, exact-channel health, text/buttons, Task-088 media upload and SSRF controls, channel-bound receipts/status, ambiguous-write behavior, subscription lifecycle, secret verification, foreign-channel/timestamp rejection before dedup and duplicate replay; provider report covers all thirteen Task-064 checks.
